column3: Imagine you're on the last train home,
and every phone in the carriage screams at the same time.
Then the train stops. Dead. In the middle of the tunnel.
Missile launch detected. Impact in twelve minutes.
Nine strangers. One locked train. Somebody starts prying at the doors.
Nobody touches those doors!
The conductor. Thirty years on this line, and she isn't shaking.
We're forty meters under the street. This is the safest place in the city.
Then your sister texts.
There's no basement in my building. What do I do?
Nine stops away. Fourteen floors up. Nowhere to hide.
Only one passenger hasn't moved. Grey hoodie. Silver case. And he's watching you.
There's a door two hundred meters back. A real shelter. Blast doors. Clean air.
It seals at impact. I can't carry this alone.
Nobody leaves this train.
There's a phone line in there. You could call Nora.
You never told him her name.
He's already cranking the emergency door open.
Do you stay on the train with the conductor, or follow the stranger into the dark?
Follow for part two.
